subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Corrosion: Chemical Attack on Metals
description: One-minute skill: Corrosion: Chemical Attack on Metals.

hook.text: Rust eats through car bodies, bridge cables, and ship hulls. Corrosion costs the world over two trillion dollars each year.

buildup.text: Iron reacts with oxygen and water to form iron oxide — rust. The oxide flakes off, exposing fresh metal. The cycle repeats.

discovery.text: Chromium in stainless steel forms a thin oxide layer that sticks. It seals the surface and stops further corrosion — passivation.

twist.text: Stress corrosion cracking combines tension and corrosion. Together they cause failures far below either individual threshold.

climax.text: Engineers fight corrosion with coatings, cathodic protection, alloy selection, and design. The battle never ends.

punchline.text: Metal wants to return to ore. Corrosion is nature recycling.

quiz.question: How does chromium protect stainless steel from rust?
options: Chromium is harder than iron so it physically blocks oxygen from reaching the surface
It forms a thin, self-healing oxide layer that seals the surface — passivation
Chromium reacts with water to create a waterproof barrier around the steel
